pl-l4d6c6-d1e115.summary: States that all who come to baptism must profess their faith and say what they seek from the Church. Asked 'what have you come to seek from the Church?', an adult answers for himself, 'faith', that is, the sacrament of faith, and teaching; asked about each article he answers that he believes in Father and Son and so on. If it is an infant unable to believe or speak, another answers for him.
claims: Adults profess their own faith at baptism.

pl-l4d6c6-d1e118.summary: Quotes Isidore: infants who cannot yet speak or believe are baptized with another professing for them, as is done for the sick, mute, or deaf; so too with penitents. But if another answers for one who can answer, it does not avail.
claims: Another may profess for those unable to speak.
Not for one who can answer himself.

pl-l4d6c6-d1e127.summary: Explains in what sense 'I believe' or 'I ask for faith' is said for an infant: of the sacrament of faith, which he is said to seek when brought to the Church and to have when baptized; 'I ask for faith' means 'I am ready to receive the sacrament of faith'.
claims: What is said for an infant refers to the sacrament of faith.

pl-l4d6c6-d1e131.summary: Quotes Augustine: to believe is to have faith; so when it is answered that an infant believes, who lacks the affection of faith, it is answered that he has faith through the sacrament of faith, and turns to God through the sacrament of conversion.
claims: An infant has faith through the sacrament of faith.

pl-l4d6c6-d1e140.summary: Raises a further question: in what sense is it answered for an infant 'I believe in God the Father, in Jesus Christ, and in the Holy Spirit'? If of the sacrament of faith, why are the persons distinguished? If of the affection of faith, how is it true when the infant lacks it? Or is it promised that he will do so when grown, as he promises to renounce the devil's pomps; if he does not, will he or the sponsor be bound?

pl-l4d6c6-d1e143.summary: Answers that what is promised for the infant is that, if he comes of age, he will renounce the devil's pomps and hold sound faith, whose sacrament he then receives. The infant is bound by this promise, not the sponsor, provided the sponsor does what he can to see it fulfilled, since diligent care is required of the godparent for the one he answered for.
claims: The sponsor promises the child's future faith and renunciation.
The child, not the sponsor, is bound.
The sponsor must take diligent care.

pl-l4d6c6-d1e146.summary: Quotes Augustine: you made a most certain pledge when you promised to renounce the devil's pomps.
claims: Baptismal renunciation is a binding pledge.

pl-l4d6c6.summary: Teaches that all who come to baptism must profess their faith and state what they seek: adults answer for themselves, 'faith', meaning the sacrament of faith and teaching; for infants, the sick, the mute, and the deaf, another answers, as Isidore says, but not for one who can answer. When it is said for an infant 'I believe' or 'I ask for faith', the sacrament of faith is meant, as Augustine says. When the sponsor answers that the infant believes in Father, Son, and Spirit and renounces the devil's pomps, he promises what the child will do when grown; the child, not the sponsor, is bound, provided the sponsor does his best to see it kept.
claims: Those coming to baptism must profess faith.
Another answers for infants and those unable to speak.
An infant 'believes' by receiving the sacrament of faith.
The sponsor promises what the child will do; the child is bound, the sponsor must take diligent care.
